Methodological assessment of clinical scoring systems reveals significant practical and physiological limitations when applied to specific quality indicators, such as [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]. Evaluations of established risk stratification tools highlight a persistent tension between comprehensive data collection and routine clinical utility. For instance, both [[p-possum|P-POSSUM]] and [[apache|APACHE]] are assessed as being too comprehensive and complex for practical, everyday use in connection with Indikator 5 [^src1]. 

Furthermore, alternative scoring methods present their own methodological blind spots. The [[surgical-apgar-score|Surgical Apgar Score]], while potentially simpler to administer, is critiqued for excluding risk patients who do not exhibit physiological stress during the perioperative period [^src1]. Together, these assessments underscore the ongoing challenge in clinical auditing of finding a risk adjustment tool that is both pragmatically feasible for clinical staff and methodologically inclusive of all relevant patient risk profiles.

## Claims

- P-POSSUM og APACHE vurderes som for omfattende til praktisk brug i forbindelse med Indikator 5 [^src1] (p-possum, apache, indikator-5)
